# Archeological Monument of the Year in Latvia

Archeological Monument of the Year in Latvia is an annual nomination of culturally and historically significant Latvian archeological site selected by the Latvian Association of Archaeologists.
The purpose of the category is to provide informative resources to the widespread public about the selected location, as well as to promote the optimization of the surrounding infrastructure, and tend to the historical monument. The underlying cause is also to raise awareness about the archeological monuments as an important parts of the Latvian culture, landscapes, and spiritual values of Latvians. The 2025 nomination invited the public to think about issues such as the accessibility of the archaeological monument, the destruction of archaeological sites, as well as the impression created by misinformation about ancient sites and cultural monuments per Mārcis Kalniņš, chairman of the Board of the Latvian Archaeological Society
The selection has been held since 2014.
Selected archeological monument by the year
* 2026 – Hillfort of Grebi [lv] and Bļoda Hill of Grebi [lv]
* 2025 – Lagzdīne Hillfort (also called Lagzdiene, Lagzdiena, or Lagzdīna Hillfort) [lv]
* 2024 – Abora I settlement [lv]
* 2023 – Livonian Sacrifice Caves [lv]
* 2022 – Cēsis Old Town
* 2021 – Aizkraukle Hillfort [lv] with the old town of Aizkraukle
* 2020 – Āraiši lake fortress
* 2019 – Atašiene Hillfort [lv]
* 2018 – Tanīss Hillfort or Hill of Tanīss [lv]
* 2017 – Mežotne Hillfort or Viesturs' Hill [https://www.arheologubiedriba.lv/aktulkais/2017/07/31/par-2017-gada-arheologijas-pieminekli-izsludinats-mezotnes-pilskalns-ar-senpilsetu lv] with the old town of Mežotne
* 2016 – Grobiņa archeological ensemble [lv]: Grobiņa Hillfort (Hill of Skārbarži) and the old town of Grobiņa, and flat ancient burial sites of Smukumi, Atkalni and Priediens, as well as hill-like ancient burial sites of Priediens and Porāni
* 2015 – Hill of Riņņi
* 2014 – Veckuldīga Hillfort [lv]
